description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between Accuracy@1 and the number of child nodes (tree width) for two models, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. The x-axis is labeled "Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)" and features a linear scale ranging from 1 to 7, with tick marks at intervals of 2. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy@1 (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 15 to 35, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The line representing GPT-4o is a solid blue line with solid circle markers; it begins at a value of 24.4 at an x-value of 1, increases to 28.9 at x=3, reaches a peak of 34.4 at x=5, and then declines to end at 31.1 at x=7. The line representing Claude-3.5-Sonnet is a solid light blue line with 'x' cross markers; it starts at 26.7 at x=1, rises slightly to a peak of 27.8 at x=3, decreases to 24.4 at x=5, and continues to decline, ending at a minimum value of 20.0 at x=7.
caption_used: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (RIGHT) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with GPT-4o peaking at 31.1% and Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforming GPT-4o across all tree widths.
